circuitpython_binary_sha256_note: The sha256 of the pinned oracle binary AS IT WAS ON DISK when this capture was last recorded: cmods/bin/circuitpython-oracle-10.3.0, 2026-09-17. The oracle moved off cmods/bin/circuitpython that day because that path is what cmods/build_interpreters.sh's cp-unix target installs, at the coverage variant's own 14-voice ceiling, and it overwrote the oracle twice (audiodsp#89); the lines below are unchanged from 2026-09-09 and reproduce on the new binary byte for byte. This is the build pinned in tests/test_voice_ceiling_consistency.py -- the two agree. It is CircuitPython 10.3.0 built at CIRCUITPY_SYNTHIO_MAX_CHANNELS=64: the same version and the same ceiling this port ships, which is the only configuration that can answer whether we render CircuitPython's bytes in the same situation. The previous capture was 10.2.1 at 14 (b3063621c72a085b, kept at cmods/bin/circuitpython-oracle-10.2.1); at that ceiling no material could be both above the knee and oracle-identical, and the above-knee half of this gate was advisory. It is not any more -- ours and the oracle are byte-identical on every line of this probe, above the knee and below. See docs/correctness-standard.md.
circuitpython_stdout_note: The pinned CircuitPython 10.3.0 oracle's own answer at N=64, captured 2026-09-09 with --capture-reference (4ec5718 took 10.3.0's synthio and audiomixer behaviour; the first capture, 2026-09-06, was 10.2.1 at N=14). ADVISORY except for the below_knee lines, which the gate does enforce -- below the knee the port and the oracle are byte-identical (measured on all three runtimes), so that check cannot fail while `stdout` matches. Its one real job is as an anti-launder tripwire: re-capture `stdout` under a changed ceiling and the full-stdout check goes green again while this one goes red, because the oracle field was not re-captured.
micropython_stdout_note: ADVISORY cross-runtime record: cmods/bin/micropython at N=64, captured 2026-09-06. Byte-identical to `stdout` on every line, which is the expected result and is worth having written down. CI cannot check this -- no runner has the binary.
stdout_note: ENFORCED, and it is THIS PORT's output -- not the CircuitPython oracle's. Above the knee the two cannot agree: the port ships CIRCUITPY_SYNTHIO_MAX_CHANNELS=64 and the pinned oracle is built at 14, and SYNTHIO_MIX_DOWN_SCALE = 0x0fffffff / (32768 * N - 28000) is 129 at 64 and 623 at 14, multiplying every sample past the knee. No material can be both above the knee and oracle-identical while those two numbers differ, so the above-knee half of this gate is enforced against the port and NOT against the oracle. The divergence is the ceiling and nothing else. See src/synthio/__init__.h's ceiling comment block; the deviation itself is not yet recorded in docs/upstream-diff.md (open with Brad, 2026-09-06).
stdout_sha256_by_arch_note: Empty on purpose. `stdout` was captured on x86_64. If another architecture (ubuntu-24.04-arm in CI) produces a different digest, it is not excused by a tolerance -- it gets its own exact accepted baseline here, with the hash, the date and the evidence, recorded only after a human has read the deviation report. Same rule and same shape as effects_component.json's cpython_stdout_sha256_by_arch (Brad, 2026-09-02: bit-identical within one architecture, not across). This probe has never been run on ARM.
what_this_is: The one parity gate whose material crosses the synthio mix-down limiter's +/-28000 knee, so that a change to the voice ceiling cannot ship green. Every other parity capture in this repository is byte-identical at any ceiling value. See audiodsp#27, tests/parity/verify_mixdown_knee.py and tests/parity/mixdown_knee_probe.py.
